one_line: Maratha Peshwa and master of mobile cavalry campaigning during the 1727–1728 Palkhed campaign against Nizam-ul-Mulk.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s, lean and athletic, with the wiry build of a seasoned horseman.
appearance.face: Oval face with sharp cheekbones, medium brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed black mustache, thin sideburns, a small tilak-shaped scar at the right temple, and a focused, alert default expression as if constantly reading the battlefield.
appearance.hair: Black hair tied in a tight top-knot hidden under a dark indigo Maratha-style turban (pagadi) with a slight forward tilt, plain except for a single modest silver crescent ornament pinned above the left eyebrow line.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha tunic with a wrapped front and side-ties, over which sits a fitted dark red quilted cotton coat (zabit or padded armor) with narrow vertical stitching and plain brown leather edging, paired with deep indigo churidar trousers tightly gathered at the ankles, a broad brown leather belt with a simple brass buckle, and a saffron cotton sash (patka) wrapped around his waist and trailing slightly to his left; his feet are in pointed brown leather mojari shoes with minimal stitching, and he has a plain steel bangle on his right wrist and small unobtrusive silver studs in both ears.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved Maratha tulwar with a steel hilt and knuckle-guard, housed in a plain brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn slung from his left hip on a cross-belt so the hilt angles forward and is always within easy reach.

ref_desc: Peshwa Bajirao I is a late-20s lean cavalryman with medium brown complexion, sharp features and mustache, wearing a dark indigo pagadi, off-white angarkha under a dark red quilted coat, deep indigo churidar, saffron sash, brown mojari, and a brown-scabbarded tulwar at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Peshwa Bajirao I as a historically grounded Maratha commander in 1727–1728: a late-20s, lean and athletic man with medium brown Deccan complexion, oval face, sharp cheekbones, straight nose, neatly trimmed black mustache, thin sideburns, and a small tilak-shaped scar on his right temple, his default expression focused and alert as if assessing terrain. His black hair is tied in a tight top-knot hidden under a dark indigo Maratha-style pagadi turban with a slight forward tilt and a single modest silver crescent ornament pinned above the left eyebrow line. He wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha tunic with wrapped front and side ties, covered by a fitted dark red quilted cotton coat (padded armor) with narrow vertical stitching and plain brown leather edging; his lower body has deep indigo churidar trousers gathered tightly at the ankles, a broad brown leather belt with a simple brass buckle, and a saffron cotton sash (patka) wrapped around his waist with one end trailing slightly on his left. His feet are in pointed brown leather mojari shoes with minimal stitching, and he has a plain steel bangle on his right wrist plus small silver stud earrings. His signature weapon is a slightly curved Maratha tulwar with steel hilt and knuckle-guard in a plain brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, slung from his left hip on a cross-belt so the hilt angles forward; show him from front, side, and back to clearly depict the dark indigo turban, off-white angarkha, dark red quilted coat, deep indigo churidar, saffron sash, brown leather accessories, and the exact positioning of the tulwar.
